You need to do that: 

So the OAuth round-trip always actually completes on now.were.cooking. That means:
APP_BASE_URL=https://now.were.cooking/ — this is what @auth0/nextjs-auth0 uses to build the redirect_uri it sends to Auth0.
Auth0 dashboard Allowed Callback URLs must include https://now.were.cooking/auth/callback to match.
were.cooking only needs to appear in Allowed Logout URLs (since logout can send you back to the marketing page) and doesn't need to be in Web Origins, since it never makes a direct auth request — it just issues an HTTP redirect at the edge.
</pasted_content id="40fa">

Then `fetch(url.toString())` resolves the hostname a second time. A domain with a very short TTL can answer a public IP the first time and `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254` the second time. Gemini returns the URLs and the publisher pages can be attacker-controlled, so this reopens the SSRF hole (§13) the module exists to close. Fix: pin the address you checked. Connect through an undici `Agent` with a custom `connect.lookup` that returns only the already-validated address, and keep the Host header and SNI set to the original hostname.\n\n- [medium] `src/lib/current-user.ts:25`: `DEV_USER.id` (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`) is returned whenever `authDisabled` is true, but no migration or seed ever inserts it into `users`. With a real `DATABASE_URL` and no `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, every write that references the user fails its foreign key: `persistOriginal` (recipes.user_id), `createSession`, `setDiscoveryCache`. Every search candidate then shows up as `fetch_failed`, and \"Start cooking\" returns 500. Fix: in the `authDisabled` branch, run `INSERT INTO users (id, auth0_sub, email, display_name) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` once, for example memoized in a module-level promise.\n\n- [medium] `src/app/api/recipes/search/route.ts:116`: `if (stop()) return;` runs before `await persistOriginal(...)`, but `shown++` only runs afterwards, at `:145`. With 5 workers, several can pass the check while `shown` is still below `maxResults`. All of them then persist and emit a candidate. For example, with `maxResults=1`, two workers finish `processExtracted` at the same moment and both stream a candidate, so the client gets more results than it asked for. Fix: reserve the slot synchronously before the await, with `if (shown \u003e= body.maxResults) return; shown++;` (or a separate `reserved` counter), and release it if the persist fails.\n\n- [medium] `src/lib/http.ts:60`: `ndjsonResponse` has no `cancel()` handler and passes no abort signal to `producer`. `SearchStream` aborts the previous search each time the user submits again. Meanwhile the other workers keep fetching up to 12 publisher pages and running extraction, which may include the Gemini fallback, with nobody reading the results. That wastes rate-limit budget and API cost. The IPv4 list also leaves out `100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT, which holds the metadata service on some clouds), and NAT64 `64:ff9b::/96` isn't decoded. A client that sends malformed bodies, such as empty text, drains the per-user 60/min budget and gets 429s on valid requests. `recipes/search/route.ts` has the same ordering. Fix: validate the body first, then check the rate limit.\n\n- [low] `src/server/cook/finish.ts:92`: this rebuilds a `PantryItem` from raw rows by hand, about 30 lines. It duplicates `rowToPantryItem` in `src/server/recipes/pantry-view.ts` and loses fields, using `expiryDate: null` and `allergenTags: []`. ### 10.7 Auth0 and Tiger quick facts

- **Auth0 free plan:** up to 25,000 MAU, unlimited social connections, 1-day log retention, no Pro MFA ([Auth0 pricing](https://auth0.com/pricing)).
- **Auth0 dashboard URLs** for production:
  - Allowed Callback URLs: `https://<domain>/auth/callback`
  - Allowed Logout URLs: `https://<domain>`
  - Allowed Web Origins: `https://<domain>`
  - Keep the localhost equivalents for dev.
- **Tiger free services:** two free services per account (beta), hosted in `us-east-1`, with **no connection pooling, replication, tiering or VPC**. A free service goes read-only when it hits its storage limit ([create a service](https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/get-started/quickstart/create-service)). That limit is reported as **750 MB** by a third party ([Bytebase, VERIFY](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/postgres-hosting-options-pricing-comparison.md)).
- **Tiger trial:** a **$1,000 / 30-day trial** of the paid tiers needs no credit card ([Tiger pricing docs](https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/about/latest/pricing-and-account-management)).
- **Provisioning:** the Console "Download the config" is **the only time the password is shown**.
- **Tiger CLI and MCP** ([Tiger blog](https://www.tigerdata.com/blog/five-features-tiger-cli-you-arent-using-but-should)):
  ```bash
  curl -fsSL https://cli.tigerdata.com | sh && tiger auth login
  tiger service create --name mise-db
  tiger db connection-string
  tiger mcp install claude-code          # lets each Claude agent inspect schema/queries
  tiger service fork <service-id> --name mise-staging   # instant zero-copy fork for migration tests
  ```

---

## 11. Gesture state machine (owned by A)

No published thresholds exist for kitchen gesture control. Every number below is an **engineering starting value to tune**, exposed in `GestureConfig` and adjustable in Settings ("Sensitivity", "Hold time", "Swipe direction", "Always armed").

### 11.1 Mapping

| User control (confirmed) | Gesture | Fires | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| *(opt-in)* Arm | `Open_Palm` held ≥ **600 ms**. Only when "Always armed" is **off**; it is **on by default** (Jerry, 2026-11-07) | `ARM`, armed for **5 s**. The window extends after each action | When enabled, stirring, chopping and reaching never fire commands. With the default, 800 ms holds, confidence thresholds and the hold-still check guard against misfires |
| Next / previous step | **`Pointing_Up` = next, `ILoveYou` (🤟) = previous**, held ≥ **800 ms**, while armed | `NEXT_STEP` / `PREV_STEP` (once per hold) | Built-in classifier gestures. Swipes and a custom landmark-based sideways point both failed in webcam tests |
| Scroll up / down | `Thumb_Up` / `Thumb_Down` held | First tick at **600 ms**, then every **700 ms** while held, each scrolling **40% of the viewport** | Avoids up/down swipes, which collide with stirring and reaching |
| Start / pause step timer | `Closed_Fist` held ≥ **800 ms**, score ≥ **0.8** | `TIMER_TOGGLE` (once per hold) | Distinct pose. A long hold and high score guard against a fist around a spoon handle |
| Read step aloud / stop | `Victory` held ≥ **800 ms** | `SPEAK_TOGGLE` (once per hold) | Rare in kitchen motion. (ILoveYou is used for previous step: the only other unused built-in gesture) |

Recognizer options:
- `runningMode: 'VIDEO'`, `numHands: 1`.
- `cannedGesturesClassifierOptions: { scoreThreshold: 0.6, categoryAllowlist: ['Open_Palm','Closed_Fist','Thumb_Up','Thumb_Down','Victory','Pointing_Up','ILoveYou'] }`. The option comes from the [1.2.2 types](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mediapipe/tasks-vision).
- The engine applies `minScore = 0.7` (and 0.8 for the fist).
